  herdr is the default transport when present:
  the worker runs in a watched pane, so a person
  can follow it live; otherwise the call blocks
  until the Unit settles. Run a long call
  backgrounded (`run_in_background: true`) and
  wait for the harness's own completion
  notification — do NOT use `ScheduleWakeup` or
  polling.

  That wait rule is for a `fgos run` call, which
  blocks until the Unit settles. `fgos workflow
  start` returns at once with the `workflowRunId`
  and a `detached` block (`pid`, `logPath`,
  `statusCommand`) while the run continues in a
  detached process: its output is never the
  result, so poll `fgos workflow status
  <workflowRunId>` until the run is `completed`,
  `failed` or parked at a gate. `answer` and
  `resume` return the same way; pass
  `--foreground` only when the caller must wait
  in place.
